entities.name: Cold War Era
entities.label: Timeframe
entities.summary:
The Cold War Era, spanning approximately 1947 CE to 1991 CE, represents a pivotal period of geopolitical tension and ideological confrontation between the United States and its Western allies, and the Soviet Union and its satellite states. This global standoff, characterized by proxy wars, an arms race, and intense espionage, profoundly reshaped international relations and the internal policies of numerous nations. It stands as a defining sub-period of the broader Contemporary era within the Annals of the World's historical classification system (division 961).

Key events marking this era include the Berlin Blockade (1948-1949), the Korean War (1950-1953), the Cuban Missile Crisis (1962), and the Vietnam War (1955-1975). The development of nuclear weapons by both superpowers initiated an unprecedented arms race, leading to the doctrine of Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD). Technological advancements during this time also spurred the Space Race, exemplified by Sputnik 1 (1957) and the Apollo 11 moon landing (1969). The period was also characterized by decolonization movements, often caught between the two competing blocs.
